clue.text: Husband meets priest left behind in the terminal

indicators.note: behind places the word for left after the husband and priest pieces

parts.note: Eli is the priest of Shiloh in the Book of Samuel
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A man joins a clergyman who has been abandoned somewhere in an airport building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left behind' reads as one phrase meaning abandoned; split it, so 'left' gives PORT and 'behind' puts it last.
explanation.definitionFit: A heliport is a landing station for helicopters, a kind of transport terminal.

clue.text: Oriental attendant who, in Paris, sits inside the coach

indicators.note: sits inside places the French word within the other pieces

parts.note: E for east, the Orient
a page is a young attendant
qui is French for who

explanation.surface: An Eastern servant, French-speaking, rides in the carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: An equipage is a horse-drawn carriage with its attendants, a coach and its outfit.

clue.text: Lack of foresight, using state's capital to support road set-up

indicators.note: to support in a down clue puts the capital beneath the road
set up in a down clue means lifted upwards, so the road is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, read here as MI
Providence is the capital of Rhode Island

explanation.surface: Poor planning means using the state capital to fund a road project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' turns MI (the M1 motorway) into IM; 'to support' puts PROVIDENCE under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvidence is failure to provide for the future, a want of prudence.

clue.text: Neat, yet at first sight a fool — a contradictory figure

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, of which an ox is one

indicators.note: at first sight points to the opening letter of the word yet

parts.note: a moron is a fool

explanation.surface: Tidy, yet looking at first like an idiot: a paradox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy but is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxymoron is a figure of speech joining contradictory terms, like bittersweet.

clue.text: Become discoloured, rather like a mountain lake?

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
the suffix -ish means rather like

explanation.surface: Is going stained a bit like a mountain lake?
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish is to lose lustre, as silver dulls and stains.

clue.text: Shrink from using counterfeit lire to protect business

indicators.note: to protect means wrapping round, so the faked lire surround the business
counterfeit means faked, so the letters of lire are reformed

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: Avoid using forged Italian money to shield a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counterfeit' makes REIL from lire, which wraps CO.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to draw back in fear or disgust, to shy away.

clue.text: A pound of tobacco

explanation.definitionFit: British slang gives a pound as a quid, and a wad of tobacco for chewing is also a quid.

clue.text: Cheerful lawmaker accepts note from beautiful youth

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the note goes inside

parts.note: gay in its old sense means cheerful
the Medes, with the Persians, made laws that could not be altered

explanation.surface: A jolly legislator receives a message from a handsome young man.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Ganymede was a beautiful Trojan boy carried off to be cupbearer to Zeus.

clue.text: An old fountain like this in the yard

indicators.note: in places the words for like this inside the yard

parts.note: an area is a sunken yard in front of a basement
thus means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A fountain of this sort stands in a courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: AREA, the sunken yard in front of a basement, is a British sense. Arethusa was a nymph turned into a fountain in Syracuse.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the nymph Arethusa became a spring, a classical fountain on the island of Ortygia.

clue.text: Heave a mound of earth, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to lift and carry something heavy
a rounded rise, of which a mound of earth is one example

explanation.definitionFit: To lug a load is to heave it, and a bump or hillock in the ground is a rounded swelling.

clue.text: Harold and May in love could create spiteful pleasure

indicators.note: could create says the letters before it are made into something new, rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A romance between Harold and May might produce some malicious fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only a link; the fodder is HAROLD, MAY, IN and O (love as nil).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, from Roman gladiatorial games, means enjoyment taken in others' suffering.

clue.text: Fashionable container of French perfume, giving off a glow

parts.note: in means in fashion
a can is a container
de is French for of
scent is perfume

explanation.surface: A trendy bottle of French fragrance shines.
explanation.definitionFit: Incandescent means glowing with heat, as a filament does.

clue.text: Counsellor's son's chair

definitions.meaning: a type of turned American armchair with a rush seat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Counsellor' is a character's name, not a lawyer or adviser: the novel Lorna Doone gives Sir Counsellor Doone a son called Carver.
explanation.definitionFit: Carver Doone is the villainous son of Counsellor Doone in Lorna Doone, and the Carver is a seventeenth-century armchair style.

clue.text: Foolish woman, some say, in the compound

indicators.note: some say tells us the words are heard as speech, not written

parts.note: a silly Kate, a daft girl given a typical name

explanation.surface: Some claim a silly girl is involved in the mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A silicate is a chemical compound of silicon, oxygen and a metal.

clue.text: Retirement cover for existing theologian

indicators.note: for here means providing a place for, so the existing word gives room to the theologian

parts.note: being is the state of existing
DD, Doctor of Divinity, a theology degree

explanation.surface: A clergyman working on in retirement covers for a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' means going to bed, so the cover is bedclothes. 'for' acts as the container signal: existing makes room for the theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets and blankets are what cover you when you retire for the night.

clue.text: Make a report when player gets sack

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football or rugby
to fire is to sack

explanation.surface: A footballer is dismissed and reports it.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine backfires with a loud bang, a report being the noise of a shot.

clue.text: Horse leaves coast road in hardened snow

indicators.note: leaves says the horse letter departs from the coast road

parts.note: a corniche is a road along a cliff face by the sea
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: A horse strays off the seaside road into packed snow.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is drug slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornice is an overhanging ledge of wind-packed snow on a ridge.

clue.text: Deferential Sabine represented in Holy Writ

indicators.note: in places the rearranged Sabine inside the scripture letters

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, part of Holy Writ

indicators.note: represented means shown again in a new form, so the letters of Sabine are rearranged

explanation.surface: A respectful Sabine woman appears in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges Sabine; Holy Writ gives the Old Testament abbreviation, which wraps the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisant means showing obeisance, bowing respectfully.

clue.text: Councillor once admitted to composing music

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so once goes between the councillor and to

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A councillor at one time confessed to writing music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' looks like part of 'Councillor once' (a former councillor) but supplies its own letters; 'composing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a piece of music for soloist and orchestra.

clue.text: By following a sudden fancy, Eliot thought the world would end with one

definitions.text: Eliot thought the world would end with one

indicators.note: following puts the word for by after the fancy

parts.note: a whim is a sudden fancy
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: On impulse, T. S. Eliot decided the world would end quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: T. S. Eliot's The Hollow Men ends 'not with a bang but a whimper'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliot's poem says the world ends with a feeble cry rather than a bang.

clue.text: Sectarian dispute about replacement of hostelry

indicators.note: about means going round, so the dispute word surrounds the rest

parts.note: a clash is a quarrel

indicators.note: replacement of says the letters of the hostelry word are moved into a new order

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry

explanation.surface: A religious quarrel concerns rebuilding a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement of' rearranges the hostelry word, and 'about' has the dispute go round that result.
explanation.definitionFit: Clannish describes a closed, exclusive group, like a sect wary of outsiders.

clue.text: Be a natural element in this place

parts.note: here means in this place

explanation.surface: To be a native part of this location.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhere is to exist as an essential, built-in quality of something.

clue.text: They go out while play is in progress

definitions.text: They go out while play is in progress

parts.words: They go out while play is in progress
parts.note: a Latin stage direction telling several actors to leave the stage during a play

explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt is the stage direction for actors departing, Latin for they leave.

clue.text: Accuse them, if wrongly, and brave the consequences

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of the preceding words are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A falsely accused person must accept the outcome bravely.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means accepting punishment or the unpleasant results of one's actions.

clue.text: Nonsense, mate!

definitions.meaning: slang for rubbish talk, as in poppycock

explanation.definitionFit: Cock means drivel in British slang, and is also a familiar greeting to a friend, like pal.

clue.text: Hines almost abandoned New York

indicators.note: abandoned says the New York letters are dropped from the word for almost

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: Someone named Hines nearly walked out on New York.
explanation.walkthrough: N and Y come out of NEARLY from separate places. Earl Hines was an American jazz pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Hines was a celebrated jazz pianist, so his given name identifies him.

clue.text: Bill leaves Aintree, possibly, for this resort

indicators.note: leaves says the bill letters go out of the racecourse word

parts.note: Aintree, near Liverpool, is a racecourse, home of the Grand National
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A bill left at the racecourse leads to a fallback.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the English racecourse that hosts the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: Recourse is something turned to for help, a resort as in last resort.

clue.text: Share books retained for circulation

indicators.note: retained means held within, so the share word keeps the books inside

parts.note: a ration is an allotted share
OT, the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A portion of books is kept back for a lending library.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotation means turning round and round, as circulation goes in a loop.
